papers.abstract: High harmonic generation (HHG) in solids typically produces a rigid frequency comb locked to exact integer multiples of the drive photon energy. In strongly correlated materials, however, the light field can dynamically transform the electronic state on the timescale of harmonic generation itself, potentially violating this rule. Here, we report giant blueshifted, non-integer HHG in a cuprate Mott insulator Sr$_2$CuO$_3$ produced by mid-infrared excitations. Concurrent transient reflectivity measurements and time-dependent exact-diagonalization simulations of a driven Hubbard model support a many-body temporal gating mechanism that suppresses light emission on the trailing edge of the pulse, thereby blueshifting radiated harmonics in the frequency domain. Our findings establish HHG emission energy as a sensitive probe of quantum many-body dynamics and pave the way for exploration and manipulation of correlated electronic phases of matter with strong-field spectroscopy.

papers.relevance_reason: This combines measurements in a cuprate Mott insulator with many-body simulations to identify a new strong-field response of correlated electrons.

papers.method_en: The authors measure high-harmonic emission and transient reflectivity during mid-infrared excitation of Sr2CuO3. They compare the observations with time-dependent exact-diagonalization simulations of a driven Hubbard model.

papers.result_en: The emitted harmonics are giant, blueshifted, and not locked to exact integer multiples of the drive photon energy. papers.abstract: Recently, two modes of spin wave excitations (magnons) were detected in Raman scattering spectra of MnTe2. It is an unconventional magnet that features a pyrite-type crystal structure hosting a non-collinear, non-coplanar antiferromagnetic (AFM) spin order below the Néel temperature. In this brief communication, the focus is primarily on the effect of spin ordering on lattice dynamics (phonons) that has been established through temperature (5 - 300 K), linear polarization angle (0 deg - 360 deg) and external magnetic field (up to 16 T) dependent measurements. It has been found that below the magnetic transition temperature, the frequencies of four out of five Raman-active lattice vibrations (i.e., Eg and three Tg phonon modes) revealed significant departure from the mechanism of the three-phonon anharmonic decay described by Klemens model. Here, we propose a new model considering spin-phonon coupling to explain frequency renormalization of the phonon part of the Raman spectrum upon the para-/antiferro- (PM/AFM) magnetic phase transition change in MnTe2. Through employing Green's function formalism, we show that a simple two-sublattice collinear antiferromagnet approach follows well both spin ordering induced hardening and softening of phonon modes observed in AFM phase of MnTe2 upon cooling. Additionally, the detailed temperature and field dependences of the energy for both magnon modes are presented. In addition to unexpected twofold anisotropy of the higher energy magnon mode (approx. 3.5 meV) unveiled in crossed configuration, our magneto-optical measurements revealed a subtle, yet definite softening trend for the lower energy mode (approx. 2.6 meV). Although the precise reasons for these effects remain unclear, we put forward a symmetry reduction in the local atomic surroundings as a possible mechanism for discussion.

papers.abstract: Spin space groups (SSGs) describe magnetic crystals in the limit of negligible spin-orbit coupling, where spatial and spin rotations decouple. Although algebraic enumerations of SSGs exist, their abstract mathematical approaches obscure the physical meaning of the resulting classifications, leaving the direct correspondence between SSGs and real-space magnetic orders unestablished. Here, we present a physically motivated framework for enumerating and classifying SSGs based on their translation holonomy---the image of the spatial lattice translation group under the spin homomorphism. The three classes of abelian images in $SO(3)$ divide SSGs into three basic translation types. Translation holonomy constrains the spin operations associated with point-group elements, yielding a complete enumeration of SSGs organized by a physical hierarchy. Within this framework, translation holonomy classifies SSGs and magnetic orders into 17 universal spin-lattice types, each with unambiguous Bragg-peak geometries and polarization signatures in neutron diffraction. Beyond organizing known magnetic orders, this framework directly predicts four universal physical phenomena: (i) exact magnetization compensation enforced by certain spin-lattice types; (ii) an exact group-theoretic criterion for the emergence of noncommuting Brillouin zones; (iii) a new type of 3Q magnetic order with vanishing octupoles; and (iv) the realization of strictly collinear momentum-space spin textures protected by reflection-staggered coplanar spin lattices. We also construct a spin space group database organized according to this physical hierarchy.
papers.physics_advance: A translation-holonomy framework organizes magnetic orders into 17 spin-lattice types and predicts, among other effects, a new 3Q order with vanishing octupoles and strictly collinear momentum-space spin textures protected by specified magnetic symmetries.
papers.relevance_reason: This is original theory of magnetic crystal orders that connects spin-space-group classification to observable diffraction signatures and predicts new magnetic phenomena.
papers.summary_zh: 本文在自旋轨道耦合可忽略的极限下，提出一种以平移 holonomy 为基础、将群结构与实空间磁序联系起来的自旋空间群（SSG）物理分类。该层级体系归纳出 17 种普适的自旋—晶格类型，并将其与中子衍射特征及若干预测的磁学现象相联系。
papers.method_en: The authors classify SSGs by the image of the spatial translation group under the spin homomorphism, distinguishing three classes of abelian images and deriving constraints on spin operations associated with point-group elements. They use this framework to enumerate SSGs, organize magnetic orders, and construct a database with diffraction geometries and polarization signatures.
papers.method_zh: 作者依据空间平移群在自旋同态下的像对 SSG 进行分类，区分三类阿贝尔像，并推导点群元素对应的自旋操作所受约束。作者据此枚举 SSG、组织磁序，并构建包含衍射几何特征和极化信号的数据库。
papers.result_en: The framework yields a complete enumeration organized by a physical hierarchy and classifies magnetic orders into 17 universal spin-lattice types with unambiguous Bragg-peak geometries and neutron-polarization signatures. It further predicts exact magnetization compensation for certain types and gives a group-theoretic criterion for noncommuting Brillouin zones. The authors also identify a 3Q magnetic order with vanishing octupoles and a route to strictly collinear momentum-space spin textures protected by reflection-staggered coplanar spin lattices.
papers.result_zh: 该框架给出按物理层级组织的完整枚举，并将磁序归为 17 种普适的自旋—晶格类型，各类型对应明确的布拉格峰几何特征和中子极化信号。它还预测某些类型具有严格的磁化补偿，并给出非对易布里渊区出现的群论判据。作者进一步指出一种八极矩为零的 3Q 磁序，以及由反射交错的共面自旋晶格保护严格共线动量空间自旋纹理的可能性。
papers.future_en: A valuable follow-up is to apply the classification and database to concrete magnetic materials and test the predicted diffraction and polarization signatures. Experimental or computational examination of the four proposed phenomena would also establish how broadly the framework’s predictions are realized.
papers.future_zh: 后续可将该分类体系和数据库应用于具体磁性材料，并检验其预测的衍射与极化特征。对所提出的四类现象开展实验或计算检验，也有助于确定该框架的预测在多大范围内能够实现。

papers.abstract: The low-field Hall resistivity of non-magnetic metals has an intrinsic quantum contribution that derives from the field-corrected Berry curvature and intrinsic magnetic moment of the Bloch states near the Fermi surface. However, its effect is usually overshadowed by the classical Lorentz-force contribution. Here we show that for the longitudinal Hall effect, which occurs in ferroaxial crystals when the applied magnetic field lies in the Hall plane, the Lorentz force contribution vanishes for the eight ferroaxial groups with a 3,4 or 6-fold rotation axis. This provides an opportunity to measure the quantum correction in isolation, but so far all measured instances of the effect fall in the remaining five ferroaxial groups of lower symmetry, where the Lorentz force dominates the signal. We compile a list of candidate ferroaxial metals with such high-order rotation axis and compute the Hall effect from first principles for representative candidates, identifying Ni$_3$P with $σ^{\rm H}_{xzx} = 28.4$ S/m/T as a promising material to unambiguously measure the intrinsic longitudinal Hall effect.
papers.physics_advance: For ferroaxial metals with three-, four-, or six-fold rotation axes, symmetry eliminates the Lorentz-force contribution to the longitudinal Hall effect, enabling a cleaner measurement of its intrinsic quantum contribution; Ni3P is predicted as a candidate.
papers.relevance_reason: The paper develops an intrinsic Berry-curvature-related Hall response in ferroaxial metals and identifies a concrete material candidate where symmetry can suppress the classical background.

papers.result_en: For the eight ferroaxial groups with 3-, 4-, or 6-fold rotation axes, the Lorentz-force contribution to the longitudinal Hall effect vanishes when the applied field lies in the Hall plane, potentially exposing the intrinsic quantum correction. The abstract notes that measured examples so far belong to the five lower-symmetry ferroaxial groups, where the classical contribution dominates. First-principles calculations identify Ni₃P as a promising high-symmetry candidate and give σᴴₓzx = 28.4 S/m/T.

papers.abstract: The celebrated Aubry-André-Harper model undergoes a metal-insulator transition akin to Anderson localization due to an energetic competition between nearest-neighbor hopping and a quasiperiodic on-site potential. In this work, we consider the problem of a one-dimensional lattice subject to a quasiperiodic external field, where the topology of the underlying graph mediates the competition between insulating and conducting phases. In particular, we present examples for which all dispersive eigenstates are critically localized, as well as models in which they are exponentially localized. We also demonstrate the coexistence of these phenomena with an extensive set of degenerate finitely supported eigenstates forming a flat band. Finally, we construct models with exactly solvable mobility edges arising only from graph structure. papers.abstract: The hexagonal altermagnet $α$-MnTe combines a near-room-temperature collinear order with a strongly spin-split electronic structure, yet the microscopic origin of its easy-plane anisotropy, its zone-center magnon gap and its anomalously large magnetostriction have remained unexplained. We derive the complete low-energy magnetic Hamiltonian of $α$-MnTe from first principles, combining density functional theory and dynamical mean-field theory with a force-theorem evaluation of the full anisotropic intersite exchange, single-ion terms and classical dipolar couplings. The isotropic exchange, including the altermagnetic splitting of the tenth-neighbor coupling, agrees with inelastic neutron scattering data. Contrary to the common single-ion picture, we find that the easy-plane anisotropy and the magnon gap at $Γ$ are governed by classical dipole-dipole interactions, which enhance the zone-center magnon splitting threefold leading to quantitative agreement with experiment, while the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya term is irrelevant despite its size. The same Hamiltonian reproduces the chiral magnon splitting along antinodal directions, mirroring the electronic spin splitting, and quantitatively accounts for the giant magnetovolume coupling of $α$-MnTe through the volume dependence of superexchange.

papers.summary_en: The paper compares spin-group and magnetic-group symmetry selection rules for nonlinear photocurrents in compensated ferrimagnetic GaFeO₃, distinguishing the limits without and with spin–orbit coupling (SOC). papers.abstract: Optical excitation offers a contact-free, ultrafast route to charge and spin currents, with symmetry determining which nonlinear photocurrents are allowed and whether they carry charge, spin, or both. Spin-group symmetry describes the limit without spin-orbit coupling (SOC), whereas magnetic-group symmetry accounts for SOC. We show that the two descriptions yield different selection rules for both charge and spin photocurrents in the multiferroic compensated ferrimagnet GaFeO$_3$. Without SOC, only linear shift and circular injection currents are allowed, with identical components for charge and spin, so every charge current is spin polarized along the moments. SOC leaves these charge currents nearly unchanged, activates magnetic linear injection and circular shift charge currents, and enables pure spin currents polarized perpendicular to the moments. Ferroelectric switching reverses the linear shift and circular injection charge currents and their spin polarization. These findings establish the importance of magnetic-group symmetry for a complete description of nonlinear charge and spin photocurrents in compensated ferrimagnets.

papers.abstract: Optical excitation has emerged as a powerful tool for manipulating and creating non-equilibrium phases of matter. Yet, the pathways available for optical control are intrinsically limited by the symmetries and interactions of the equilibrium system. Here, we demonstrate that these pathways can be redesigned through atomic-structural engineering to access hidden dynamical properties. By combining resonant vibrational excitation with epitaxial strain, we realize a light-induced, room-temperature multiferroic state in strained thin films of the technologically relevant hexagonal ferrimagnet, barium hexaferrite (BaFe$_{12}$O$_{19}$, BaM). Time-resolved second harmonic generation and magneto-optical Kerr effect measurements reveal an enhanced ferroelectric polarization together with a weakening of the magnetic moment upon exciting mid-infrared phonons in strained BaM thin films, but not in the bulk material. Structural analysis and first-principles-based theory show that this effect is enabled by strain-generated displacement of Fe$^{3+}$ ions, which break the local symmetry and facilitate an emergent dynamical magnetoelectric coupling. Both the strong lattice excitation and strain-induced symmetry breaking are essential for enabling this dynamical coupling, promising an important template for designing otherwise inaccessible non-equilibrium phenomena.

papers.announcement_time_basis: arXiv dated batch and official 20:00 Eastern release schedule

papers.summary_en: Local compressibility measurements in Bernal-stacked pentalayer graphene resolve symmetry-broken Landau levels and interaction-driven transitions between subbands. The transitions show hysteretic Hall responses whose magnitude and sign can be tuned by displacement field.
papers.summary: In two-dimensional electron systems, strong Coulomb interactions can spontaneously lift flavor degeneracies such as spin and valley, producing first-order transitions with hysteretic switching of interest for memory devices. The subband degree of freedom in multiband systems may be viewed as a flavor that not only participates in such transitions but also enables control of the hysteretic behavior
papers.abstract: In two-dimensional electron systems, strong Coulomb interactions can spontaneously lift flavor degeneracies such as spin and valley, producing first-order transitions with hysteretic switching of interest for memory devices. The subband degree of freedom in multiband systems may be viewed as a flavor that not only participates in such transitions but also enables control of the hysteretic behavior, as a displacement field can shift the energy difference between subbands. Here, we demonstrate this principle in Bernal-stacked pentalayer graphene, whose low-energy spectrum comprises a monolayer-like Dirac sub-band together with light and heavy bilayer-like sub-bands. Local compressibility measurements resolve a fully symmetry-broken Landau-level spectrum and a sequence of phase transitions that occur when Landau levels of different subbands cross, at which strong interactions redistribute the occupation among flavors. We show that these transitions exhibit hysteretic Hall responses in magnetic field, confirming their first-order character, and that the magnitude and sign of the hysteresis are tuned by the displacement field, as expected from the subband Landau-level ordering determined in compressibility measurements. Our work establishes the subband degree of freedom in multiband systems as a resource for engineering hysteretic switching, and highlights how local thermodynamic measurements can link microscopic insights to macroscopic responses in quantum materials.

papers.abstract: We study the spectrum of arrays of critical transverse field Ising chains perturbed by a weak inter-chain coupling in the scaling limit, using an exact diagonalization algorithm based on Hamiltonian truncation. As the number of chains is made large, we confirm the existence of excitations below the two particle continuum that can be identified with the celebrated Zamalodchikov $E_8$ theory with small corrections. In addition, we find a distinct $ψ$-particle, with mass $M_\mathrmψ$ which is not contained in the $E_8$ theory. Its ratio to the lowest $E_8$ mass ($M_1$) is a universal number, which we have computed numerically to be $M_\mathrmψ/M_1 = 1.819\cdots$ for a one dimensional array of critical chains. We present evidence that this new state fundamentally involves excitations on neighboring chains, explaining why it has no analogue in the single chain problem. Interestingly the $M_\mathrmψ$ mass has a characteristic scaling dependence on detuning from the critical point that is qualitatively distinct from the $E_8$ masses, which can help identify it in spectroscopic experiments on easy-axis magnetic chain materials.

papers.abstract: Despite extensive experimental and theoretical studies of quadrupolar order in Ba$_2$MgReO$_6$, the microscopic origin and relative energy scales of the interactions driving it remain unresolved. In particular, the observed ferroic ordering of the $z^2$ quadrupole has remained difficult to explain, as the relative contributions of superexchange, classical quadrupole-quadrupole interactions, vibronic couplings, and virtual excitations to higher-energy levels have not been established quantitatively. Here, we determine all these interactions from first principles and solve the resulting microscopic Hamiltonian. The calculated ground state reproduces the experimentally observed quadrupolar order parameters and the associated structural distortions with quantitative accuracy. Disentangling the individual contributions, we find that ferroic $z^2$ order originates from a linear-quartic coupling, generated by virtual excitations to the $J_{\mathrm{eff}}$= 1/2 doublet and driven by vibronic interactions. Our results establish the hierarchy of microscopic interactions underlying quadrupolar order in Ba$_2$MgReO$_6$ and provide a unified $ab \ initio$ description of its coupled electronic and lattice degrees of freedom.

papers.abstract: The kagome superconductors AV3Sb5 (A=K, Rb, Cs) host multiband superconductivity (SC) within an unconventional charge density wave (CDW) parent phase, yet the relationship between the two remains unresolved. Through time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (tr-ARPES) experiments on CsV3Sb5 and KV3Sb5, we observe coherent band oscillations driven by coupling to a low-energy CDW amplitude mode at 3.1 THz. We find this coupling to be highly band-selective, differing by a factor of over 2 even between bands with dominant V-3d character. We reproduce these results with frozen-phonon density functional theory calculations, offering insight towards the relation between differing Fermi surface characters and our observed band selectivity. Furthermore, we observe differences in coupling channels between KV3Sb5 and CsV3Sb5. These results establish CDW amplitude mode fluctuations as a band-selective low-energy coupling channel that intimately contributes to the interplay between CDW and SC in the AV3Sb5 compounds.

papers.abstract: A perpendicular electric field can reorient a momentum-space spin texture without changing the local magnetic configuration. In this Letter, we investigate this mechanism in a $21^\circ$-twisted $\mathrm{NiPS}_3$ bilayer with zigzag order and coplanar, nonparallel layer Néel vectors. In the ideal nonrelativistic limit, an antiunitary in-plane half-translation enforces opposite-spin pairing at opposite momenta, while a layer-exchanging twofold operation pins the leading $p$-wave spin splitting to a crystallographic direction. A perpendicular layer bias lifts this orientational constraint while preserving the antiunitary symmetry, allowing a transverse component of the splitting vector. First-principles calculations show gate-dependent reorientation and deformation of spin-resolved isoenergy contours. Wannier-based linear-response calculations further reveal field-activated diagonal spin conductivities and a polarity-dependent tilt in the angular profile of the transverse spin-current response. The spin-texture axis, dispersion axes, and transport-response axis are distinct quantities governed by the same symmetry reduction. These results identify layer bias as a route to controlling odd-parity spin textures and spin-current anisotropy, provided that the coplanar magnetic state remains stable.

papers.authors: P. J. F. Cavalcanti, M. D. Croitoru, A. I. Buzdin
papers.summary_en: The paper derives the superconducting response of a spin-orbit-coupled thin film to a Néel domain wall, focusing on spontaneous currents, vortex pinning, and vortex–antivortex nucleation. It finds that sufficiently strong magnetoelectric coupling can favor a bound vortex–antivortex pair even without an applied field.

papers.abstract: We study the superconducting response induced by a Néel domain wall in a thin superconducting film proximity-coupled to a ferromagnetic layer in the presence of interfacial Rashba spin-orbit coupling. The combined action of the magnetic texture and broken inversion symmetry generates a magnetoelectric coupling that induces spontaneous equilibrium currents. To establish the basic response to a continuously rotating magnetic texture, we first consider a periodic harmonic cycloid as an analytically tractable reference problem. Near Tc, this reference problem illustrates how the magnetoelectric coupling modifies the superconducting order parameter, while below Tc it provides a simple setting for describing the phase response, Pearl screening, and the interaction with a vortex. We then turn to the main problem of this work, a single Néel domain wall, and derive analytical expressions for its equilibrium phase profile, spontaneous current, magnetic field, and vortex-wall interaction energy.We show that the Néel wall acts as an extended magnetoelectric source and produces a vorticity-selective pinning landscape controlled by the competition between the wall width and the effective screening length. We further demonstrate that sufficiently strong magnetoelectric coupling can render a bound vortex-antivortex pair energetically favorable relative to the vortex-free state, even in the absence of an applied magnetic field. Our results provide an analytical framework for understanding magnetoelectric vortex pinning and vortex-antivortex nucleation by Néel domain walls in spin-orbit coupled superconducting films.
papers.physics_advance: A Néel domain wall creates a vorticity-selective vortex-pinning landscape and, at sufficiently strong magnetoelectric coupling, can make a bound vortex-antivortex pair favorable without an applied field.
papers.relevance_reason: This is a substantive theoretical study of superconducting films, predicting how magnetic texture and spin-orbit coupling generate currents and alter vortex energetics.

papers.authors: Justin Schirmann, Martin Rodriguez-Vega, Alexander Cerjan
papers.summary_en: The paper establishes that a fully gapped class-D superconductor can support Majorana flat bands without chiral symmetry or time-reversal symmetry when the gap is odd under a mirror and translation along the edge is preserved. It develops a model that also exhibits end and corner Majorana modes and applies a real-space spectral localizer to finite samples.

papers.abstract: Majorana flat bands, zero modes across the whole edge Brillouin zone, usually rest on chiral symmetry. We show that a fully gapped class-D superconductor can host such a flat band without chiral symmetry or time reversal, provided its superconducting gap is odd under a mirror and translation along the edge is preserved. Combined with particle--hole conjugation, the mirror forms an antiunitary antisymmetry that squares to $+1$ and preserves the momentum along the edge, so it fixes the Kitaev index of every slice of fixed edge momentum. In a gapped bulk, this slice index cannot change with the edge momentum, and the edge zero modes form a band across the whole edge Brillouin zone. We construct a four-band model with exactly these symmetries, a helical $p$-wave superconductor with Rashba coupling in an in-plane exchange field, from which no term can be removed without restoring an additional symmetry. On the mirror lines, its two mirror sectors are exact Kitaev chains. This yields a closed-form phase diagram. Besides the flat band, the model hosts a phase with two Majoranas at each end of a wire, although its class-D index is trivial, and a second-order phase with Majorana corner modes. The spectral localizer detects all these indices in real space, directly on finite-size samples as relevant for experiments. On open rectangular flakes of two widths, it reproduces the phase diagram even though translational symmetry is broken. In the nodal regions, its reading depends on the flake size, so they are left unread. The readings persist under disorder several times the bulk gap. Without translation along the edge, the symmetries protect no more than Majorana parities, and we quantify the signatures that remain specific to the antisymmetry. A minimal model of magnetic adatoms on a triplet superconductor realizes the flat-band and second-order phases.
papers.physics_advance: A mirror combined with particle-hole conjugation can protect Majorana flat bands in a fully gapped class-D superconductor without chiral symmetry or time-reversal symmetry, and the framework also yields wire-end and corner Majorana phases.
papers.relevance_reason: This is an original theoretical result identifying symmetry conditions for topological superconducting edge and corner states beyond the usual chiral-symmetry mechanism.
papers.summary_zh: 本文指出，当超导能隙在镜面对称下为奇且边缘方向的平移对称性得以保持时，完全有能隙的 D 类超导体即使没有手征或时间反演对称性，也可支持 Majorana 平带。作者构建的模型还呈现端点和角落 Majorana 模，并将实空间谱局域化子用于有限尺寸样品。
papers.method_en: The authors combine mirror and particle–hole symmetries to formulate the relevant antisymmetry, and construct a four-band helical p-wave model with Rashba coupling and an in-plane exchange field. They use a spectral localizer to identify indices and phases in finite rectangular flakes, including under disorder, and present a magnetic-adatom model as a possible realization.
papers.method_zh: 作者结合镜面对称与粒子—空穴对称性建立所需的反对称性，并构造包含 Rashba 耦合和面内交换场的四带螺旋 p 波模型。研究使用谱局域化子识别有限矩形薄片中的指标与相（包括无序条件下），并提出磁性吸附原子模型作为可能的实现方案。
papers.result_en: The combined mirror–particle-hole antisymmetry fixes the Kitaev index for every edge-momentum slice, yielding a flat band across the edge Brillouin zone; the model also has a phase with two Majoranas at each wire end despite a trivial class-D index, and a second-order phase with corner modes, with localizer readings persisting under disorder several times the bulk gap.
papers.result_zh: 镜面对称与粒子—空穴对称构成的反对称性固定每个边缘动量切片的 Kitaev 指标，从而在整个边缘布里渊区形成平带；该模型还具有每个线端存在两个 Majorana 模但 D 类指标平凡的相，以及具有角落模式的二阶相，而谱局域化子的读数在强度达体能隙数倍的无序下仍保持。

papers.abstract: Electron-phonon coupling (EPC) plays a vital role in the electrical and optical properties of materials, ranging from superconductivity to charge dynamics. In moiré superlattices, out-of-plane vibrations can modulate the moiré potential and enhance interlayer EPC. Here we report the first direct observation of a resonance arising from coupling between moiré electronic excitations and phonons in graphene-based moiré superlattices. Using Fourier-transform infrared photocurrent spectroscopy, we detect the nominally silent hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) out-of-plane optical (ZO) phonon as a pronounced absorption peak. The phonon interferes with moiré flat-band excitations to form a characteristic Fano resonance. Displacement field-dependent measurements confirm that the feature originates from coupling to the moiré electronic continuum rather than simple zone folding. We further observe similar resonances in devices with different graphene layer numbers and twist configurations. This enhanced EPC provides a pathway for understanding and controlling emerging quantum phenomena, such as superconductivity, and engineering novel optoelectronic devices.
papers.physics_advance: Observes a Fano resonance between the hBN out-of-plane optical phonon and moiré electronic excitations, providing direct evidence of enhanced interlayer electron–phonon coupling.
papers.relevance_reason: The experiment directly probes electron–phonon coupling in graphene-based moiré materials and distinguishes coupling to the moiré electronic continuum from simple zone folding.

papers.abstract: Superconductivity in spin-polarized metals challenges conventional opposite-spin pairing, particularly when a magnetic field strengthens rather than suppresses it. In graphene, the additional valley degree of freedom broadens the possible pairing channels, making the valley occupation of the parent metal central to understanding such superconductivity. Here we report in-plane-field-enhanced superconductivity in hBN-aligned 17-layer rhombohedral graphene. Normal-state quantum oscillations reveal unequal Fermi pockets consistent with a valley-imbalanced, spin-polarized parent metal. Calculations show that the parent electron pocket is predominantly localized on the bottom surface and largely preserved by electrostatic screening as additional Fermi pockets emerge. Superconductivity persists in this regime but is suppressed when carriers are polarized toward the hBN-aligned surface, where the parent bands undergo strong moire reconstruction. An adjacent nonlinear metallic response evolves continuously into superconducting critical-current features and persists above the superconducting transition temperature. The combination of valley imbalance and in-plane-field-enhanced superconductivity motivates a phenomenological magnon-assisted equal-spin intervalley pairing scenario. These findings provide experimental constraints on pairing in valley-imbalanced metals and open a route to testing magnetic pairing mechanisms through layer-selective control of the parent electronic states.
papers.physics_advance: In-plane-field-enhanced superconductivity in thick rhombohedral graphene coexists with a valley-imbalanced, spin-polarized parent metal, and its dependence on layer-selective band reconstruction constrains possible equal-spin intervalley pairing.

An adjacent nonlinear metallic response evolves continuously into superconducting critical-current features and remains observable above the transition temperature.

It also characterizes the projected interaction and relaxation of this core Fermi gas.

papers.abstract: The Caroli-de Gennes-Matricon states bound to a vortex line in a clean type-II superconductor form one-dimensional minibands that disperse along the vortex. The lowest miniband is separated from the Fermi level by a minigap $E_0\simΔ^2/E_F$. A magnetic field shifts the minibands of the two spin projections in opposite directions. At the threshold field $B^*$ the Zeeman energy equals $E_0$. Estimates for FeSe place $B^*$ at a few tesla. The lowest miniband of one spin projection then crosses the Fermi level, and a spin-polarized one-dimensional Fermi sea forms inside the vortex core. We develop the theory of tunneling spectra across this Lifshitz transition. We solve the Bogoliubov-de Gennes equations numerically in the quantum limit for all momenta along the vortex and compute the local density of states with thermal and instrumental broadening. The zero-bias conductance at the vortex center is absent below $B^*$. It has a maximum near $B^*$ with the inverse-square-root field dependence of a one-dimensional van Hove singularity and decreases at higher fields. The next miniband produces a second onset at a finite distance from the center. The zero-bias signal is carried by one spin projection at the center and by the opposite one in the surrounding ring. We then project the screened electron interaction onto the filled miniband. The resulting Luttinger parameter is close to unity, so the core hosts a weakly interacting one-dimensional Fermi gas. Its quasiparticles relax through three-particle collisions in analogy with thermalization in quantum wires and at quantum Hall edges. The corresponding relaxation rates are established analytically.
papers.physics_advance: Predicts a Zeeman-driven Lifshitz transition in vortex-core minibands, producing a spin-polarized one-dimensional Fermi sea and a characteristic inverse-square-root zero-bias tunneling signal near threshold.
papers.relevance_reason: This theoretical study predicts distinctive vortex-core electronic states and tunneling signatures in a superconductor, including experimentally testable field dependence.

papers.method_zh: 作者在量子极限下对涡旋方向上的所有动量数值求解 Bogoliubov–de Gennes 方程，计算包含热展宽和仪器展宽的局域态密度，并将屏蔽电子相互作用投影到已占据的小能带上。他们还解析推导了三粒子碰撞导致的弛豫率。
papers.result_en: The zero-bias conductance at the vortex center is absent below the threshold field B*, peaks near B* with the inverse-square-root field dependence of a one-dimensional van Hove singularity, and decreases at higher fields. A higher miniband produces a second onset away from the center, while the zero-bias signal comes from opposite spin projections at the center and in the surrounding ring. The projected Luttinger parameter is close to unity, indicating a weakly interacting one-dimensional core gas whose quasiparticles relax through three-particle collisions.

papers.abstract: Phonon thermal and angular-momentum (AM) Hall effects are known in non-ferroelectric insulators, yet whether terahertz soft modes of displacive ferroelectrics, i.e., ``ferrons", share them remains open. We report axial ferrons that hold polarization-momentum locking in uniaxial ferroelectrics and show that both effects exist: a longitudinal temperature gradient drives a transverse AM flow without any field, whereas an out-of-plane magnetic field switches on the thermal Hall response. Two competitive channels emerge for the AM Hall effect: self-radiated magnetic fields hybridize two branches into circular modes whose momentum-locked Berry curvature deflects opposite magnetic moments to opposite edges, while temperature-gradient-induced mode quantum coherence adds a magnetic-moment dipole that leads to an opposite transverse AM current. An out-of-plane magnetic field breaks the exact polarization-momentum locking and yields a polarization Hall current. Numerical calculations show these effects are significant in both LiNbO$_3$ and van der Waals ferroelectrics. Edge magnetization or polarization accumulation can switch adjacent magnets or ferroelectrics, enabling low-power magnetoelectric functionality by thermal current in the future.
papers.physics_advance: Axial ferrons in uniaxial ferroelectrics can carry transverse angular-momentum flow under a temperature gradient through competing Berry-curvature and coherence mechanisms; an out-of-plane magnetic field additionally enables a thermal Hall response.
papers.relevance_reason: Theoretical predictions for collective modes in ferroelectrics establish new angular-momentum and thermal Hall responses and identify mechanisms that could be tested in material systems.
papers.summary_zh: 本文预测具有极化—动量锁定的单轴铁电体中的轴向铁子（太赫兹软模）会产生热霍尔效应和角动量霍尔效应。文章阐述角动量霍尔响应中的竞争贡献，并报告这些效应在 LiNbO₃ 和范德华铁电体中数值上显著。
papers.method_en: The authors analyze ferron modes, their Berry-curvature and quantum-coherence contributions to transverse angular-momentum flow, and their response to an out-of-plane magnetic field. Numerical calculations are presented for LiNbO₃ and van der Waals ferroelectrics.
papers.method_zh: 作者分析铁子模及其对横向角动量流的贝里曲率和量子相干贡献，并考察其对面外磁场的响应。文章针对 LiNbO₃ 和范德华铁电体给出数值计算。
papers.result_en: A longitudinal temperature gradient produces a transverse angular-momentum flow without an applied field, while an out-of-plane magnetic field activates a thermal Hall response. The angular-momentum Hall effect has two competing channels: self-radiated magnetic fields hybridize branches into circular modes whose momentum-locked Berry curvature deflects opposite magnetic moments toward opposite edges, whereas temperature-gradient-induced mode coherence contributes a magnetic-moment dipole that drives an opposite transverse current. The out-of-plane field breaks exact polarization-momentum locking and produces a polarization Hall current. Numerical calculations indicate significant effects in both LiNbO₃ and van der Waals ferroelectrics.
papers.result_zh: 纵向温度梯度无需外加磁场即可产生横向角动量流，而面外磁场会激活热霍尔响应。角动量霍尔效应包含两种相互竞争的通道：自辐射磁场将两个分支杂化为圆偏振模，其动量锁定的贝里曲率使相反磁矩偏向相反边缘；温度梯度诱导的模态相干则产生磁矩偶极，并驱动方向相反的横向电流。面外磁场会破坏严格的极化—动量锁定，并产生极化霍尔流。数值计算表明，这些效应在 LiNbO₃ 和范德华铁电体中均显著。

papers.abstract: The spin-1/2 XXZ antiferromagnet on the triangular lattice in a magnetic field is a paradigmatic frustrated quantum magnet, yet its ground-state phase diagram at generic anisotropy and its thermal phase structure remain incompletely understood. Here, using infinite density-matrix renormalization group, infinite projected entangled-pair operator, and exponential tensor renormalization group methods, supported by exact diagonalization, we resolve both issues. At zero temperature, we map the phase diagram continuously from the Ising limit to the Heisenberg point and find that the nonclassical $Ψ$ supersolid is a stable phase just below saturation at all anisotropies studied: it borders the one-third-magnetization up-up-down plateau directly in the strongly easy-axis regime and the semiclassical $V$ phase toward the Heisenberg point. In the strongly easy-axis regime, we uncover an intrinsically finite-temperature bond-nematic phase above the zero-temperature plateau--$Ψ$ boundary, in which the three bond directions become spontaneously inequivalent without transverse spin coherence or three-sublattice order. A hard-core-boson mapping reveals its origin: once thermal fluctuations destroy phase coherence, the field-doped holes settle on domain walls of the local up-up-down order, which are stabilized by quantum kink delocalization and aligned by its $Z_3$ registry. Our results call for reexamining high-field states in triangular-lattice cobaltates such as Na$_2$BaCo(PO$_4$)$_2$ and K$_2$Co(SeO$_3$)$_2$.

papers.result_en: At zero temperature, the Ψ supersolid is stable just below saturation at all studied anisotropies. In the strongly easy-axis regime, it borders the one-third-magnetization up-up-down plateau directly, whereas toward the Heisenberg point it borders the semiclassical V phase. The authors also find a finite-temperature bond-nematic phase above the zero-temperature plateau–Ψ boundary, with inequivalent bond directions but no transverse spin coherence or three-sublattice order. The proposed hard-core-boson account attributes this phase to doped holes occupying domain walls of up-up-down order after phase coherence is lost, with quantum kink delocalization and Z3 registry alignment stabilizing the walls.
papers.result_zh: 在零温下，所研究的各向异性范围内，饱和磁场以下均存在稳定的 Ψ 超固相。在强易轴区域，该相与磁化率为三分之一的 up-up-down 平台直接相邻；趋近海森堡点时，则与半经典 V 相相邻。作者还发现，在零温平台相与 Ψ 相的边界之上存在有限温度键向列相，其不同键方向不等价，但没有横向自旋相干性或三亚晶格序。硬核玻色子图像将该相解释为：相干性消失后，掺入的空穴占据 up-up-down 有序的畴壁；量子 kink 离域和 Z3 注册关系对齐则有助于稳定这些畴壁。
papers.future_en: The phase diagram motivates renewed examination of high-field states in triangular-lattice cobaltates, including Na2BaCo(PO4)2 and K2Co(SeO3)2, as stated in the abstract. Further material-specific comparisons could test whether the predicted finite-temperature bond-nematic phase is realized in those systems.
papers.future_zh: 正如摘要所指出的，该相图促使人们重新考察三角晶格钴酸盐（包括 Na2BaCo(PO4)2 和 K2Co(SeO3)2）中的高场态。进一步开展针对具体材料的比较，可检验所预测的有限温度键向列相是否会在这些体系中实现。
papers.tier_reason_en: The work combines a broad anisotropy-dependent phase diagram with a potentially novel finite-temperature phase and a microscopic account, using multiple complementary numerical methods. It is a substantial theoretical result, but its conclusions are computational and the abstract does not report experimental confirmation, supporting a strong specialist-journal tier rather than a broader one.

papers.abstract: The field-induced spin supersolid of the square-lattice $S=1$ antiferromagnet with single-ion and exchange anisotropy has so far been characterized only by static observables, among them a two-peak transverse structure factor. We compute its dynamic spin structure factors, and those of the neighboring phases, by stochastic analytic continuation of stochastic-series-expansion quantum Monte Carlo data on a $16\times16$ lattice at inverse temperature $β=32$, at one field in each of the supersolid, the $m_z=1/2$ Ising plateau and the canted $XY$ phase. The supersolid has a single Goldstone mode, which the checkerboard folds onto both the ordering wave vector $\mathbf{Q}=(π,π)$ and $\mathbf{q}=(0,0)$, so that it appears in both spin channels at both points with one velocity $v=1.36\pm0.01$. The canted phase shows half of this pattern and the plateau none, the latter carrying instead a gapped magnon band and a two-magnon longitudinal continuum. Exactly at $\mathbf{Q}$ and $(0,0)$ the finite-lattice spectra are governed by a rotor tower of the condensate in the transverse channel and an Ising doublet of the checkerboard in the longitudinal one, both present at $\mathbf{Q}$ in the supersolid. Three parameter-free comparisons with the stiffness and the uniform susceptibility of the same runs, for the velocity, the sound-mode weight and the thermal decay of the rotor tower, tie the continued spectra to raw Monte Carlo observables. The folded Goldstone mode is the dynamical fingerprint of the supersolid.
papers.physics_advance: The supersolid's checkerboard order folds its single Goldstone mode onto both the ordering wave vector and zero momentum, producing a characteristic pattern absent in neighboring phases.
papers.relevance_reason: This original quantum-magnetism study predicts dynamical signatures of a field-induced spin supersolid in a square-lattice antiferromagnet.

papers.abstract: Twisted bilayer graphene (TBG) is commonly viewed through two limiting regimes: strongly correlated flat bands near the magic angle and nearly decoupled Dirac cones at large twist angles. Here we explore the intermediate regime. Using hyperbolic plasmon-phonon polaritons (HP$^{3}$) to probe the dynamical electronic response, we investigate bilayer graphene from AB stacking to $5.5^\circ$ TBG. We identify a narrow density window in which the HP$^{3}$ wavelength becomes strongly gate tunable. The window opens when doping suppresses Landau damping and a coherent graphene plasmon emerges. It closes at a second crossover, which appears only above $4^\circ$ and shifts systematically with twist angle. Continuum-model and electrodynamic calculations trace this second crossover to hybridization between the central and remote moiré bands, which weakens the density dependence of the Drude response. The resulting polaritonic tunability is concentrated within a twist-angle-selected density window and produces total wavelength changes approaching $90\%$. Our results demonstrate that remote moiré bands reshape the collective electrodynamics of TBG far from the magic-angle regime and establish large-angle TBG as a platform for gate-reconfigurable mid-infrared polaritons and material cavities.
papers.physics_advance: Remote moiré-band hybridization produces a twist-angle-dependent crossover that limits the density tunability of graphene polaritons at large twist angles.
papers.relevance_reason: Experiments and modeling reveal how moiré-band physics in twisted bilayer graphene reshapes its collective electronic response beyond the magic-angle regime.

papers.abstract: Moiré graphene multilayers provide an atomically thin platform for engineering narrow topological bands through stacking, twist, and electrostatic control. Recent experiments on twisted rhombohedral graphene have revealed a high-Chern-number hierarchy determined by the number of rhombohedral layers. A microscopic description of this hierarchy requires connecting the ideal chiral picture to the realistic electronic structure. Here, we show that the two central moiré bands of twisted monolayer-$N$-layer rhombohedral graphene originate from hybridization between a monolayer Dirac cone and a rhombohedral surface state located at opposite corners of the moiré Brillouin zone. Increasing $N$ progressively narrows these bands, whereas reversing the displacement field transfers their wave-function weight between the twisted interface and the remote surface. In spectrally isolated regimes, this redistribution switches the lower band between Chern numbers $\mathcal{C}=N$ and $\mathcal{C}=-1$. A projected surface theory shows how interfacial tunneling is dressed by virtual propagation through the rhombohedral stack, explaining the field-selected Chern hierarchy and the recurring threefold structure of the real-space charge textures. These results establish layer number and displacement field as complementary nanoscale controls of band flatness, spatial polarization, and topology in graphene moiré heterostructures.
papers.physics_advance: It connects the central moiré bands to hybridization between a monolayer Dirac cone and a rhombohedral surface state, showing how layer number tunes band flatness and displacement-field reversal switches the isolated lower band between Chern numbers N and −1.
papers.relevance_reason: This original theory addresses moiré-band topology and electronic structure in a low-dimensional graphene material, with testable controls from layer number and displacement field.

They examine how layer number and displacement-field reversal alter the resulting bands and wave functions.

papers.result_en: The two central moiré bands arise from hybridization between states at opposite corners of the moiré Brillouin zone, and become progressively narrower as the rhombohedral layer number N increases. Reversing the displacement field transfers wave-function weight between the twisted interface and remote surface; in spectrally isolated regimes, the lower band switches between Chern numbers C=N and C=−1. The projected theory also accounts for the field-selected Chern hierarchy and recurring threefold real-space charge textures.
